belief: God can't use me without a good job.
origins: Job titles, income, and influence can seem like the qualifications for being used by God. When a layoff, health problem, or limited education leaves us without a “good job,” we may believe our usefulness has expired. Churches can reinforce this when leadership roles go mainly to the successful.
teaches: When the leaders saw the boldness of Peter and John, “realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they marveled and took note that these men had been with Jesus.” Gideon said, “my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.” Amos said, “I was not a prophet… I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.” God said to Moses, “Who gave man his mouth?” God does not need a résumé. He uses willing people.
self_statements: I have nothing to offer without a good job.
I am too ordinary to be useful.
I need a better résumé first.
Others are better suited for His work.
My unemployment makes me useless to Him.
errors: Calling myself useless because of my job status.
Overlooking gifts and character I already have.
Believing I am either useful with a good job or useless.
Measuring my usefulness against successful people.
questions: Whom did God use in Scripture who had no status?
What gifts, kindness, and wisdom do I have that no job title gives?
Who around me could I help this week?
What does “with Jesus” mean for my usefulness?
What would I tell a friend without a job who felt this way?
What is one thing God might use me for today?
truth: God does not need my job title. He uses people who have been with Jesus, ordinary and willing. I can serve right where I am today with the gifts He gave me.
hw_truths: Being with Jesus is the qualification.
He used the weakest and youngest.
My gifts do not depend on a job.
He made me as I am for His purposes.
log: Each day, write one way you helped or encouraged someone.
actions: Write ten qualities and abilities that are not job titles.
Do one act of kindness or help this week.
Share how you feel about your work situation and ask for perspective.
prayer: Father, You use ordinary people. Free me from believing I must have status to serve You. Show me someone to help today and use me where I am. Amen.
hw_questions: Whom did God use who had no status?
What would I tell a friend?
How might God use me today?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God can use ordinary people who have been with Jesus, and that includes me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “God can't use me without a good job.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
